subject: Compliance roadmap: ISO 27001 scope choices & FedRAMP readiness gaps
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Compliance roadmap: ISO 27001 scope choices & FedRAMP readiness gaps

Hi team,

As we narrow the scope for the upcoming ISO 27001 effort and align our FedRAMP readiness plan, I want to surface a few open questions before we lock owners/ timelines. High level asks below — I'm proposing a short sprint to triage these and produce a draft evidence intake plan by Mar 26.

- Scope: Should we include both Redwood-hosted and Dedicated instances (customer-managed VPC) in the initial ISO scope, or limit to hosted API + control plane? Risks: including Dedicated raises on-prem evidence collection complexity.
- FedRAMP readiness: we have a gap matrix from last year; need confirmation on KMS/HSM evidence for private deployments and timeline for bringing HSM attestation into scope.
- SIG/CAIQ: Marissa, can you confirm which questionnaires we should prioritize for Acme (they requested SIG first)?

I've attached a quick diagram that shows the proposed scope boundaries and a readiness matrix excerpt. Can each of you reply with owners, top-3 blockers, and whether we can commit to the sprint timeline?

Thanks,

Diego
Director, Security Programs
Redwood Inference
Attachments: ISO_scope_diagram.pdf (diagram, 1.2MB), FedRAMP_readiness_matrix.xlsx (sheet: gap-summary)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Compliance roadmap: ISO 27001 scope choices & FedRAMP readiness gaps

Diego — thanks for kicking this off. Quick responses and notes: 

- Scope recommendation: start with hosted API + control plane in scope for ISO baseline. Dedicated (customer-managed VPC) as "in-scope for attestations but scoped-in by exception" — meaning we document boundary and require customer evidence paths rather than full Redwood evidence collection. This reduces immediate audit friction.
- Owners: I can own SIG/CAIQ responses for Acme and shepherd the intake for hosted artifacts. Irene — would you take FedRAMP KMS/HSM evidence coordination?
- Top blockers: 1) HSM attestation timing (external vendor), 2) evidence retention mapping across Dedicated vs Hosted, 3) resourcing for evidence collection from infra (SRE) team.

I've attached a draft SIG responses doc with comments on Q1-10. I'll open a shared Google doc for collaborative edits after this thread.

Proposed next steps:
- Mar 19: 30m sync with Security, Infra, and Compliance to confirm scope and owners.
- Mar 22: Draft SIG/CAIQ initial pass for Acme.
- Mar 26: Consolidated evidence intake plan for ISO baseline.

Marissa
Senior Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference
Attachments: SIG_responses_draft.docx

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>

Cc: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 14:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Compliance roadmap: ISO 27001 scope choices & FedRAMP readiness gaps

Thanks — adding a few technical clarifications: 

- KMS/HSM: For FedRAMP, we need vendor attestation for keys used for customer data in Dedicated deployments. For hosted, our KMS rotation artifacts + access logs should suffice for initial readiness. We should identify the subset of keys that are customer-facing (used for request-level encryption) vs platform-only.
- Evidence approach: I propose an evidence "map" where artifacts are tagged by deployment type (hosted/dedicated), control family (cryptography, access control, logging), and retention window. That will make sampling requests during audit more deterministic.
- Timeline caution: SRE can support an evidence pull but will need a clear list of specific artifacts and a 72-hour lead time for complex logs.

I'll take point on the evidence map and draft a template by Mar 21 if that works. Mina — flagging you for storage retention confirmation.

Irene
Principal Security Engineer, Infrastructure Security
Redwood Inference

From: Lydia Chen <lydia.chen@cobaltsec.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Compliance roadmap: ISO 27001 scope choices & FedRAMP readiness gaps

Thank you for the summary and attachments — useful starting point. A few items from the auditor side: 

1) Pre-audit readiness: we'd like to run a 60-minute pre-audit walk-through the week of Mar 29 to understand the scope boundaries and sample availability. Please propose 2 times.
2) FedRAMP HSM attestation: when you have confirmation from the HSM vendor, please share the attestation or timeline. If the vendor cannot provide the attestation before the audit window, we can accept compensating controls but need them documented now.
3) Evidence sampling: auditors prefer a mapping table that ties each control to an artifact path and owner. If Irene can produce the evidence map by Mar 21 that would be ideal.

Proposed times for pre-audit: Tue Mar 30 10:00-11:00 PT or Wed Mar 31 14:00-15:00 PT.

Lydia Chen
Senior Auditor
Cobalt Security Assessments
